_comment: Per-robot calibration for a Feetech STS3215 Robotroller.
COPY THIS FILE before editing; do not calibrate the default in place.
Every servo value below is specific to one physical build. The values from
the Physical Atari paper are for Dynamixel XC-330 servos on a different
robot and DO NOT transfer -- neither the encoder positions nor the PID
gains. Calibrate your own; see PORTING_PLAN.md section 7.
PID: Feetech coefficients are 1-byte EEPROM values (0-254), unlike
Dynamixel's 2-byte RAM registers. The paper's 1500/6000/1500 are not
expressible here. Use -1 to leave a servo's programmed value untouched.
STS3215 factory defaults are around P=32, I=0, D=0. Start conservative:
raise P until the joystick reaches its target briskly without buzzing or
overshoot, and keep motion gentle -- the paper traced controller wear to an
over-aggressive motion profile.
dpad_lr_default / dpad_ud_default are the two dpad axes' neutral encoder
counts. They are separate because there is no reason a left/right and an
up/down servo rest on the same count unless the horns are indexed that
way -- the paper's build had both at 2048; yours probably will not.
goal_speed (steps/s) and goal_acc (units of 100 steps/s^2, where 0 means
no acceleration limiting). A ~132-count d-pad deflection takes ~55 ms at
speed 2400 / acc 0, but ~230 ms at acc 50 and ~363 ms at speed 600/acc 20 --
against a total end-to-end budget of ~165 ms. Raising goal_acc softens the
throw (the paper traced controller wear to an aggressive profile) but spends
reaction time to do it.
overcurrent_counts: high-current reflex threshold in RAW CURRENT COUNTS
(~6.5 mA per count on an STS3215), NOT milliamps. 185 counts ~= 1200 mA,
the paper's figure, but calibrate it: stall a servo by hand and read the
reported value, then set the threshold comfortably below it.
